answer: Each identity locks an 85-credit bond and posts one key-bound relic, a work sample planted as one vertex in an orchard register. A verifier recomputes it: its delta from the recomputed result must stay within 2 percent and beat the benchmark, or the bond burns. A claimed relic cannot support a second identity, so the k-th fake needs its own bond plus a 50-credit sample; 1,000 fakes cost 135,000 credits. An honest agent posts one owned relic, locking one refundable bond. A rented relic fails because the renter cannot reproduce its steps, burning the bond and flagging both.
